# Pastel 0.9.0

## Pocket: a compact list at your text cursor

  • Pocket is a small clipboard list that opens right under the text cursor in the app you're typing in. Where an app doesn't share its cursor position, it opens at the pointer. The ribbon stays on ⇧⌘V.
  • Its shortcut: new installs open Pocket with ⌃⌘V. If you're updating, Pocket starts without a shortcut, because ⌃⌘V is Paste Special in Microsoft Office: open it from the menu bar, or set a shortcut in Settings › Shortcuts.
  • Hold to cycle, like ⌘Tab: keep ⌃⌘ down and press V again to step down the list, then let go to paste. Let go after one press and Pocket stays open for searching.
  • Type to search with letters spread out: "ngxrl" finds "nginx reload". Matched letters are highlighted.
  • Paste as: press ⇥ to paste the selected item another way: one line, trimmed, quoted, as code, uppercase, plain text without formatting, a link as Markdown, its title or its domain, a color as RGB, HSL or SwiftUI, a file's path or name, or the text Pastel read in a screenshot.
  • When the intelligent clipboard is on, the item that fits what you're writing is selected, with its reason.
  • Pinboards in the current space appear as chips; switch with ← and →. ⌘1–⌘9 paste by number, ⇧↵ pastes plain text, ⌥⌫ deletes an item, ⎋ clears the search and then closes.

## Saved links

  • Rename saved links: choose Rename… from a link's menu, or press R in the list.
  • Links saved from Zen take the names you gave their tabs in Zen's sidebar, and follow later renames there until you rename them in Pastel. Clearing a name brings back the one from Zen.

# Pastel 0.8.0

  • Resize the clipboard ribbon by dragging its top edge up or down, or use the new size slider in Settings. Double-click the handle to return to the original size. Your choice is remembered.
  • At smaller sizes, choose Compact tiles for readable titles and details or Dock icons for thumbnails with details on hover. Switch from the ribbon’s More menu or Settings. Full preview cards return as you make the ribbon taller.
  • Keyboard selection, Quick Paste, dragging, context menus and Space preview work across ribbon sizes. Sensitive items stay concealed in both compact styles.
  • Sparkle now downloads signed updates automatically by default and installs them when you quit Pastel. Settings includes separate controls for automatic checks and downloads. Existing explicit update preferences are preserved.

# Pastel 0.7.0

## A Front Page for more browsers

  • Safari now includes Pastel Front Page as a bundled extension, with your pinned bookmarks, projects and saved links in new tabs and windows.
  • Firefox has a temporary extension preview, including a new-tab dashboard and optional home page. Permanent Firefox installation still requires Mozilla signing.
  • Browser settings guide you through Safari, Chrome and Firefox setup.

## Bring your open tabs together

  • Choose which browsers to collect normal open tabs from: Safari, Chrome, Firefox and Zen.
  • Matching links merge across browsers and profiles. Existing titles, lists, pins and Done status stay in place.
  • Browser sources appear on saved links. Closing a tab keeps its saved bookmark.
  • Only current tab titles and addresses are collected. Private tabs, browser history, page contents, internal pages and credential-bearing URLs are excluded. Automatically collected links skip background page fetching and organization.

Safari must be enabled in Safari’s Extensions settings. Existing Chrome installations need the updated extension files reloaded to grant the new tabs permission. Collection starts only after you opt in for each browser in Pastel’s Browser settings.
